chunks: And from him, from Ibn Hurayth, from Amr ibn al-Hasan al-Ushnani, who said: Ahmad ibn Musa ibn Ishaq al-Taymi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).

He was asked about the visitor to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Whoever performs ritual bath (ghusl) in the Euphrates, then walks to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), for every step he raises and places, there is a accepted pilgrimage (hajj) with all its rites.'

key_terms.الزَّائِر: The visitor (to a shrine or grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn after bathing in the Euphrates?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the spiritual merit of Ziyarat al-Husayn by linking physical devotion to divine acceptance. It specifically notes that performing the ritual bath (Ghusl) in the Euphrates River before walking to the shrine transforms every step into a fully accepted Hajj, emphasizing the sanctity of the location and the act of pilgrimage in Shia tradition.
